newsitem.title: FRANCE: France handled 722,500 tonnes wheat bids Friday. [CORRECTED 11:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: France handled 722,500 tonnes wheat bids Friday. [CORRECTED 11:25 GMT]

text.p: European grain traders bid through France on Friday for 722,500 tonnes of European Union soft wheat export at a standing export tax of 0.5 Ecus per tonne, cereals office ONIC said on Monday.
They also sought licences for 9,000 tonnes of durum wheat at a fixed export tax of five Ecus, an ONIC official said.
The bids are for grain through the EU's daily export channel, a first-come-first-served system which gives the European Commission three working days to reject bids.
The channel operates on a standing level of refund or tax known as "common right". The Commission imposed common right taxes on wheat, wheat flour, durum and semolina last Thursday.

Unusually, the Commission left the door open to commercial exports through its daily channel on terms which were just as favourable as the results of its latest weekly tender, which showed a minimum tax of 0.5 Ecus per tonne for soft wheat.
The move was seen as increasing the trade's flexibility during the Commission's two-week formal absence from the market until the next tender on August 14 (corrects from August 21)
-- although it can reject bids or close the channel by raising the fixed tax at any time.
EU officials have said that unlike in previous years they are happy to release significant quantities in the first part of the season to prevent disruption from a second big annual crop.
Any excessive run on supplies is likely to bring down the shutters fairly quickly but the Commission has not said what it regards as a fair volume between now and the next formal tender.
France traditionally handles most export bids but it was not immediately clear whether traders had also used other member states to secure licences using the daily channel.
EU wheat is becoming more competitive as the dollar scales new heights against the French franc and other currencies.
Based on Monday's higher dollar and a 0.50 Ecu tax, Friday's bids valued French wheat close to $143 per tonne for September, compared with $145 for the same wheat on Thursday.

Traders noted September U.S. soft red winter was worth around $140.20 a tonne at Friday's close and was being indicated around $1.50 a tonne higher in electronic trading on Monday. --Tim Hepher, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
